features.feature_value: Remove automatically when vulgar language/inappropriate personal-directed content; allow when argument/opinion is valid.
features.evidence_span: "If there was any vulgar language or inappropriate things directed towards individuals, I automatically opted to remove."
features.rationale: The participant states a clear removal trigger (vulgar/personal-directed content) and allows otherwise.

features.feature_value: Deny posts that seem even remotely threatening, while valuing free speech.
features.evidence_span: "Anything that seemed even remotely threatening I denied posting."
features.rationale: They describe threat-detection as the primary rejection criterion despite their free-speech emphasis.

features.feature_value: Use moderation-guideline violations to decide, using both versions to apply the same standards more fairly.
features.evidence_span: "focusing on whether the content violated moderation guidelines rather than on the political viewpoint being expressed"
features.rationale: They explicitly frame their comparison approach as consistency against moderation rules rather than political stance.

features.feature_value: Weigh views across conservative-democrat and other party perspectives to justify responses.
features.evidence_span: "based on the ideologies I have a s a conservative democrat"
features.rationale: They indicate their ideology and cross-party consideration shaped their judgments.

features.feature_value: Removed item due to implying a call to violence; other controversy not enough for removal.
features.rationale: They give a specific content trigger for removal (call to violence).

features.feature_value: Reject tweets that seem outrageous plus cursing and nonsense.
features.evidence_span: "Tweets that seemed outrageous got rejected as well as cursing and nonsense"
features.rationale: They list concrete rejection cues: outrageousness/cursing/nonsense.

features.feature_value: Most posts seen as opinions; removal only if really inflammatory language, outrageous lies, or calls to action; generally OK.
features.evidence_span: "I was looking for really inflammatory language, outrageous lies, or \"calls to action\".."
features.rationale: They describe an explicit threshold for removing and claim most posts did not meet it.

features.feature_value: Perceived both comments as trying to make a point or insult.
features.evidence_span: "both comments trying to make a point or insult."
features.rationale: They characterize how the content was understood (point/insult), but do not state a moderation rule or comparison mechanism beyond that.
